pulse.currentFocus: Session 338 ran the arc under founder authorization for a direct push to main and a full production deploy, and its three findings were all gates that were not doing what their names promised. FIRST: the red uptime-probe cron was not the ordering race the board recorded. Reproduced locally, build-deploy-currency drifted between --probe and --check because observationFromReceipt() never restored the three content-clock fields added in S336 — the third time a field was added to the emitter and forgotten in the reader (after retainedForHours in S300 and historyComplete in S316). The consequence was far larger than a red cron: classify() reads contentLagHours, so every non-probe re-derive — npm run build:check, the content lane, every local build — collapsed it to null, which silently disabled the content ceiling S336 built specifically to catch a whole release stranded in production. Fixed, and the class closed with a fixed-point self-test that names no field (derive(read(derive(x))) === derive(x)) plus a companion case proving that guard can fail; 87/87, was 85. Notably an S300 test of exactly this shape already existed and stayed green throughout, because its fixtures omitted the dropped fields. SECOND: Lighthouse CI had been red for 15 consecutive runs across ~27 hours, so the site's performance gate had produced no verdict for over a day and nothing said so. /ranks/ was consolidated into /leaderboards/#ranks and answered by a _redirects 301, but three CI audit-target lists still named it — including the one auditing the LOCAL PREVIEW, which serves the built tree with no edge layer, so the redirect cannot apply and Lighthouse 404'd on a page that cannot exist there. /vaultsparked/ was in the same state. Both removed, and scripts/check-workflow-audit-targets.mjs added to build:check with two rules that name no route: no target may be a `from` in route-consolidation.json, and every local-preview target must resolve to a real page. THIRD: staging parity was a hand-maintained three-route sample and structurally could not see an absent route, which is why S337 could only record /how-we-build/ as an anecdote. It now compares the surface each origin advertises: production advertises 134 routes, staging 115, 23 missing on staging including /evidence/, /how-we-build/, three news editions and the whole .ai/ layer, with staging's build-sha reporting 94e78e93 built 2026-08-28 — five days behind production. Published as surfaceParity with gating:false and the reason stated on the artifact, because gating on a known-open blocker is a self-inflicted release outage. OUTCOME: closed out, pushed directly to main, and fully deployed to production. FOURTH, surfaced by converging the gate rather than by the audit: build-news-visual-receipts hashes each story's rendered page but ran four steps before build-shell-assets rewrote them, so it was stale by construction on every shell rotation and its own error message prescribed a hand-rebuild rather than the ordering fix; moved after every page rewriter and immediately before the seal, which also removes a confound from the standing build-to-build churn investigation. The visual and mobile proof receipts were then recaptured against the final tree: no UI changed, so CANON-053 was not triggered, but those receipts bind the candidate manifest sha rather than any appearance, and every reseal invalidates them. OUTCOME: the full production deploy LANDED. Run 33613020727 completed the release ceremony without rejection and promoted a clean dist; api/build-sha.json reports e1c7cef4b, exactly the pushed main HEAD. Eleven public routes verified 200 live with a real browser user-agent and the three consolidated routes verified 301. A live build-deploy-currency --probe followed by --check — the exact sequence that had been reddening the uptime cron — now exits 0 on both, with state current and 0 commits behind, so the content ceiling disabled since S336 is measuring again in production.
pulse.nextMilestone: Find and fix whatever refreshes the staging origin — it stopped on 2026-08-28 and is 23 advertised routes behind production — then flip surfaceParity to gating so CANON-007 stops running backwards. Then hoist the Trusted Types default-policy installer ahead of the 31 client assets that load before it and decide the founder-approved enforce flip on fresh evidence, the founder privacy decision on the four silent-zero tables, and the manual CANON-053 rendered-pixel review of the newly-served surfaces.
blockers: TRUSTED TYPES ENFORCE: blocked by a named defect, not only by stale evidence. ambient-core.bundle.js installs the TT default policy that the site's ~167 legacy innerHTML sinks depend on, and its own comment says it MUST load before any sink usage — but it is not the first script on the page. Measured across 137 built pages in S337: 31 sink-bearing assets load before it (pwa-nav.js 81 pages, pwa-install.js 72). Report-Only hides this; enforcement throws. The repair rewrites every page head and invalidates every hash-bound receipt, so it is a session of its own (D-S337.3).

identity/auth surfaces remain held on real-provider-e2e-pending (obelisk.identity.verify missing OBELISK_RP_ID/RP_NAME/RP_ORIGIN; obelisk-staging-registration missing). NOTE (S337, D-S337.1): this holds the IDENTITY BLAST RADIUS only — auth/**, surface:identity, worker:identity. It does NOT block a full production deploy: the S319 scoped path returns allowed=true mode=scoped for any candidate disjoint from that radius, and did so this session.

STAGING IS FIVE DAYS BEHIND PRODUCTION, now measured rather than anecdotal (S338, D-S338.3). check-staging-parity compares advertised sitemaps: production 134 routes, staging 115, 23 missing — /evidence/, /how-we-build/, three news editions and the whole .ai/ fact-sheet layer — and staging's api/build-sha.json reports 94e78e93 built 2026-08-28. CANON-007 makes staging the thing production is verified against, so the release ceremony's browser matrix is clearing a tree five days newer than the one it measures. surfaceParity is published with gating:false on purpose: gating on a known-open blocker would be a self-inflicted release outage. Unblock by establishing what deploys the Hetzner staging origin and why it stopped, then flip gating.

PRIVACY DECISION (founder): four public tables — challenge_submissions, game_sessions, point_events, member_achievements — have no anonymous read path, so /community/, all seven /leaderboards/* and public member profiles render zeros and empty states to signed-out visitors. The fix generalizes the S335 public_leaderboard pattern, but it decides which member activity becomes publicly readable and is escalated rather than applied (D-S336.5).

identity: the provider chain is live and verified; production promotion is held only on the real-provider journey, whose remaining leg is a founder passkey ceremony — hardware-key enrollment is founder-reserved by CANON-019 and is deliberately not automatable.

Trusted Types enforcement stays held. Founder approved the flip in S335, but api/tt-readiness.json now honestly reports stale-evidence: its soak manifest is 57 days old against a declared 30-day window. The ageing defect is fixed; the missing input is a fresh KV soak, not a code change.
rollback architecture: the GitHub Pages warm origin still follows mutable main; D-S303 requires explicit founder authorization before migrating to an immutable verified generation.
IGNIS freshness: stale in a studio-ops portfolio artifact this repo cannot write; resolve upstream rather than backdating.
The Dispatch has zero confirmed subscribers until the founder clicks the double-opt-in confirmation email.

startup-revenue-agreement is red: the promoted v5 startup brief renders a revenue evidence age the shared resolver disagrees with, and context/SIGNALS.md is stale. Studio-ops brief-renderer owned; must not be fixed by editing the sibling repo.

now: [S338][DEPLOY/P1] Refresh staging, then flip `surfaceParity.gating` to true. S338 measured it: staging is 23 advertised routes and five days behind production (`94e78e93`, 2026-08-28). The parity probe is built and reporting; it is deliberately non-gating because gating on a known-open blocker is a self-inflicted release outage. Find what deploys the Hetzner staging origin, why it stopped, and whether it is wired to any lane at all — then refresh, confirm `surfaceParity.state` reads `matched`, and set gating. Until then the release ceremony's browser matrix is measuring a tree that is five days older than the one being promoted, which inverts CANON-007. (D-S338.3)

[S338][BUILD/P2] Two more receipts may be ordered before what they observe — audit the whole `postbuild` chain for the D-S338.4 class. `build-news-visual-receipts` hashed news pages while running four steps before `build-shell-assets` rewrote them, so it was stale by construction on every shell rotation and had been quietly listed among the S335 "47 files churn between identical builds" set. Fixed by moving it after every page rewriter and immediately before the seal. Walk the rest of `postbuild` with the same question — *does this step hash or read rendered pages, and does anything after it rewrite them?* — and in particular re-check whether the remaining build-to-build churn ([S335][BUILD/P2]) is the same defect rather than a clock-relative selection window, which was the standing theory. A pinned-clock double build now has one fewer confound.

[S338][UX/P3] The home portfolio cards render a doubled status label. Observed directly in the S338 CANON-053 capture pass: each card shows a `● SPARKED` pill and, beneath it, a second orange `SPARKED` that is clipped to a bare `S` on the smaller tiles. It appears identically in dark and light at 1366px and is therefore not an animation frame, and no `SPARKED` badge exists in the static markup of `index.html` (only one unrelated prose mention), so it is rendered client-side — start at whatever writes the card status pill. PRE-EXISTING, not introduced in S338, and deliberately not fixed there: changing UI would have invalidated every hash-bound receipt immediately before an authorized production deploy. Full description is on `docs/visual-qa/LATEST.json`.

[S338][OBS/P2] Audit the other receipt round trips for the D-S338.1 class. `build-deploy-currency.mjs` now proves `derive(read(derive(x))) === derive(x)` over a fully-populated observation. Every other generator with a committed-receipt reader has the same hazard and, in at least one case, the same false comfort: an S300 structural case already existed here and stayed green for two sessions because its fixtures omitted the fields that were actually dropped. Enumerate the generators that read their own output back (`build-worker-route-history`, `build-release-proof`, `build-status-proof`, `build-citation`, `build-public-status` are the candidates), and give each the fully-populated fixed-point case plus its can-fail companion. A fixed-point test is only as wide as its fixture's field coverage.

[S337][OBS/P1] The `uptime-probe` cron is RED — and it was NOT an ordering race. S338: root-caused and fixed. Reproduced locally: `--probe` then `--check` drifted on the three S336 content-clock fields, because `observationFromReceipt()` never restored them. Reordering the `--check`, as this item proposed, would not have helped — the round trip itself was lossy. Worse than a red cron: `classify()` reads `contentLagHours`, so every non-probe re-derive collapsed it to null and the S336 content ceiling was disabled on `build:check`, the content lane and every local build. Fixed, plus a fixed-point self-test that names no field, plus a proof the guard can fail (87/87 self-test, was 85). Verified end to end: `--probe` then `--check` now exits 0 with `contentLagHours` intact. (D-S338.1) Original text: Two consecutive scheduled failures as of 2026-09-02 (runs `33593653589` 05:10:50
next: [NEXT][SIL][NEWS/AI/P1] Claim-evidence relationship map + agent critique packet. Add stable fact rows and validated factRefs joining factual evidence to stances and visual anchors; publish a per-story public-safe argument map and one-click critique packet with no runtime model spend.

[NEXT][SIL][OBS/P1] Field-vitals freshness closure. Surface observed-through/stale-days, restore a fresh post-S262 RUM window, and bind cohort verdicts to a release SHA so fresh generatedAt can never imply fresh field evidence.
